facts.fact: The Centre for Human Rights and Rehabilitation and Youth and Society wrote to MACRA's board on 17 January 2025 urging it to suspend the procurement of a social media monitoring system, citing risks to privacy and freedom of expression.
facts.system: MACRA social media monitoring system procurement

facts.fact: The Net Rights Coalition, a pan-African digital rights network, wrote to MACRA on 27 January 2025 warning that the monitoring system appeared capable of mass communications surveillance and calling for stronger safeguards.
facts.system: MACRA social media monitoring system procurement

facts.fact: A group calling itself the Concerned Citizens of Malawi People Power Movement publicly criticised MACRA by January 2026 for failing to brief the public on the monitoring system procurement.
facts.system: MACRA social media monitoring system procurement

facts.fact: Activist Manes Hale was detained in 2018 over Facebook posts concerning then-President Peter Mutharika.
Tumpale Mwakibinga was charged in 2019 under the Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act after posting criticism of the first lady on Facebook.
Ignatius Kamwanje was convicted and sentenced to 18 months' imprisonment in May 2021 over a Facebook post alleging financial misconduct at the National Bank of Malawi.
Journalist Joshua Chisa Mbele was arrested in January 2022 after sharing on Facebook a document alleging corruption involving government officials.
Police arrested 20-year-old Chisomo Makala in January 2022 after tracing a phone number used to share in a WhatsApp group a video interpreted as mocking the president.
